fields.name: Brown Recluse Zine Distro
notes: Brown Recluse Zine Distro was created to support and center zines written predominantly by POC folks of all identities. This project was born out of passion for zines and frustration at the lack of representation and meaningful zine material for People of Color. I scoured through zine distros with a fine tooth comb and found that just like everywhere else in the dominant culture there was a serious lack of material written by POC folks in these distros. This is not because there is a lack of zines written by People of Color

because there are hundreds of self-published works written by People of Color. My personal zine collection is full of POC zines and zines that are of interest to us.\r\n\r\nSo after many years of reading zines
writing zines and observing zine culture I decided to start a zine distro that centers our voices and presents our large contribution to zine and DIY culture. BRZD is dedicated to our struggles

our projects and our zines. Brown Recluse Zine Distro was born in the spirit of visibility and in the spirit of celebrating our cultures and inter-sectionality. BRZD exists to strengthen our ties and highlight out inter-sectional relateable experiences. BRZD is here to offer a place to locate POC zines without spending hours browsing the internet.

fields.name: Portland Button Works and Zine Distro
fields.address:
PBW Zine Distro
5307 N Minnesota Ave.
Portland, Oregon 97217
notes: "We are interested in zines that are based in DIY and punk ethics in regards to politics"

"and pricing. In an effort to keep zines accessible we prefer zines that are $5 retail or less.\\r\\n\\r\\nKinds of zines we are interested in:\\r\\n-Perzines that fall into the personal is political with thoughtful narratives"

"especially zines with interesting and creative design & layout that suits the writing.\\r\\n-Witchcraft zines that are not Wiccan and that are preferably secular witch friendly (also culturally sensitive"

"and do not express views of gender essentialism.)\\r\\n-Zines that cover a single issue that are well researched and explore unique topics and perspectives\\r\\n-Thoughtfully put together zines exploring self-care\\r\\n-Vegan cook zines\\r\\n-DIY project zines\\r\\n-Independently produced tarot and oracle decks\\r\\n\\r\\nKinds of zines that we are not particularly interested:\\r\\n-Comics (unless you consider it a zine and the focus is a topics listed above)"
"Chapbooks\\r\\nWe hope it goes without saying that are not interested in zines expressing views of racism"

"and all other forms of discrimination.\\r\\nIf you think your zine might be a good fit with us please send one actual physical copy for distro consideration (no digital files) to the address below with a note stating the retail price"
"and a way to contact you. If there is no note we will assume you are just randomly sending a zine and we will donate it to a zine library."

fields.name: Antiquated Future
notes: and handmade odds and ends out of Portland
Oregon. We carry over 500 items at any given time
and over 250 different zine titles.\r\n\r\nIn terms of zines
we try to carry a wide range of zines
while still maintaining a curated selection. Personal
and music are all zine genres we find ourselves especially drawn to. We also try to carry a range of zines in terms of cost and production quality—both simply designed

affordable zines (that nod to the '90s zine heyday we came up in) and high-production value art-focused zines and workbook zines that reflect where people have taken the zine format in recent years. We hope to offer a lot of entry points into falling in love with zines.

fields.name: The Word Distribution
notes: Focusing on the lighter side of things – cats
etc. Fully supportive of zine culture and all things zine related. DIY till you Die!

fields.name: Silver Sproket
notes: Silver Sprocket is a radical indie publisher
and comic shop focused on indie comics and comic zines
but we distro plenty of non-comic zines too whenever someone who works here gets excited about something.\r\n\r\nWe strive to build a better world without forgetting to have a good time.

fields.name: CRAPANDEMIC
notes: text-heavy perzine/fanzine distro for mallgoths of the internet
run out of the Midwest by julia eff & friends. Nothing over $6
with all items available on sliding scale pricing (just email/DM). We have patches & stickers & pins & stuff too. Submissions always open!

fields.name: Wasted Ink Zine Distro
fields.address: The Hive – 2222 N 16th St, Phoenix, AZ 85006
notes: WIZD was born from a deficit of creative spaces that voice the self-expressions of our desert-dwelling community. We work to highlight zines from underrepresented communities such as the POC
and disabled folks. This has led to representing 200+ zine makers and their variety of works – from comics

fields.name: Take Care
notes: Take Care was founded on 1 January 2010 by Tim and Emma
Australia. We stock zines that we've made
some by good friends and comrades
and some that we just really like. We stock perzines
travel zines and other zines that are conceptually
and that aren't overpriced. We like zines that explore intersectional anti-capitalist/communist/anarchist politics
pop-culture and everyday life. We don't currently have an open submission policy

but if you think your zine might fit really well with our current roster please feel free to get in touch – no promises though; we're just a little distro and don't have heaps of time or space to keep loads of stock 🙂

fields.name: Bus Stop Press
fields.address:
Giz c/o CIRA
50, rue Consolat
13001 Marseille
France
notes: "tapes & records since 2010. Everything on a pay what you want basis. Punkpost is encouraged but we can work around that. Original zines include the Cheaptoys & Papercore series. The distro has a permanent kiosque at the CIRA-Marseille (International Center for Research on Anarchism)."

fields.name: Pen Fight
notes: Pen Fight is a feminist and queer zine and bookshop and small press based out of Manchester
and other DIY and small-run art and craft.\r\n\r\nWe stock work on feminist and women's rights
and anything else with an ace DIY ethic.\r\n\r\nWe also operate a small press
we want to amplify the voices and creative work of the marginalised and new artists and zinemakers.

fields.name: Ohio State University Rare Books & Manuscript Library
fields.address:
Thompson Library
1858 Neil Avenue Mall
Columbus, Ohio 43210-1286

fields.name: Queer Anxiety Babiez Distro
notes: Three non-binary zinesters in the East Bay making and distributing zines focused on disability
and gender from a queer perspective. Their titles are described as very personal and raw
often mixing poetry with essays on topics like selfies
and living in a queer/disabled body.

fields.name: Archive Six
notes: Seattle-based small press and zine distributor that began as a way to distribute the personal work of its founder
and later expanded into a curated distro centering marginalized voices. Its catalog focuses on work about social justice
women of color and other underrepresented creators
with Archive Six frequently tabling at regional events like Seattle Zine Fest.

fields.name: Catland Books
notes: Catland Books is an occult bookstore and witchcraft-oriented community space in Bushwick
often described as 'Brooklyn's favorite witch shop.' The shop carries a mix of occult and esoteric books
and independently produced zines and small-press titles related to witchcraft

fields.name: Darcy Crash Distro
notes: Darcy Crash Distro is a zine distro project (active primarily online

via social platforms) that publishes and distributes personal and political zines. Posts and mentions show Darcy Crash collaborating with Brown Recluse Zine Distro on events such as fundraising for Zine Queens Vol. 3
indicating strong ties to QTBIPOC-centered and feminist zine communities. The distro's work leans into themes of trauma

fields.name: FIST Zine
notes: FIST is a New York-based queer erotic and intimacy-focused zine project and event series that publishes themed print issues (e.g.
' 'FIST Issue 04: Devotion') and related works like 'Linked
A Polyamory Zine.' Its site sells print issues and tickets to events such as 'Bawdy
and erotic art centered on queer desire and kink.

fields.name: Homie House Press
notes: Homie House Press is a radical cooperative small press and 'photo book' platform founded by Adriana Monsalve and Caterina Ragg
dedicated to equipping historically underrepresented people with the tools to create and publish in the photobook and zine medium. Described by its founders as a 'sisterhood
' and 'secret space and open house for honest content
' the press views itself as a visual recording project that prioritizes community over everything

fields.name: Last Gasp
notes: Last Gasp is a San Francisco-based publisher and former distributor of underground comix
founded by Ron Turner in 1970 in Berkeley. Over five decades it became one of the oldest and most influential houses for underground comics and radical graphic culture
and an array of art books

fields.name: Radiator Comics
notes: Radiator Comics is a Chicago-born small-press distributor and publisher dedicated to self-published and small-press comics
founded in July 2014 by Neil Brideau. Its primary focus is distributing mini-comics and graphic stories by over 200 emerging and independent cartoonists
offering an online storefront plus tabling at festivals such as Small Press Expo and Chicago Alternative Comics Expo (CAKE).

fields.name: Stranger Danger Zine Distro
notes: Stranger Danger Zine Distro was a Chicago-based zine distro that specialized in feminist
widely cited in zine-community guides as a go-to source for radical personal and political work. It carried titles focused on feminism
and anti-authoritarian politics. In a 2019 Instagram post
the distro announced that Stranger Danger had come to an end.

fields.name: Pioneers Press
notes: Pioneers Press was an independent publishing house and small-press distributor founded in 2012 by Jessie Duke after leaving Microcosm Publishing
Michigan and a distribution center on a farm outside Leavenworth
Kansas. The press focused on survival and sustainability in rural and urban settings
and literary work by emerging authors. Pioneers Press operated as both publisher and distro but closed on December 31

fields.name: Flywheel Arts Collective
notes: Flywheel Arts Collective was a volunteer-run multi-use art and meeting space in Easthampton
located at 43 Main Street (in the old town hall) with a performance venue
and zine library. Active through the 2000s and 2010s
Flywheel hosted punk and experimental music shows

fields.name: Doris Press
notes: Doris Press is the long-running personal-as-political zine imprint of Cindy Crabb
publisher of the influential perzine Doris
which has been produced since the early 1990s. The press also published the 300-page Encyclopedia of Doris: Stories
collecting work from the zine into a bound volume while keeping the DIY ethos intact. In a zine-ecosystem map
Doris Press serves as a key perzine publisher focused on trauma

fields.name: McMicken FreeSpace
notes: volunteer-run community space and zine distro housed in a formerly foreclosed building on West McMicken Avenue in Cincinnati
envisioned by founder Stephanie Kodakya Phillips as a safe
accessible 'freespace' for people without a foundation. Evolving from an earlier project called SoapBox Books and Zines
it now serves as Cincinnati's only explicit activist hub and solidarity center
hosting groups like Cincinnati Allied Transgender Support
and AA for Freethinkers/Art of Recovery.

fields.name: Microcosm Publishing
notes: Microcosm Publishing is a Portland-based zine publisher and distributor founded in 1996
originally in Cleveland before relocating to Portland
empowering books and zines about DIY skills
and radical politics. Emerging from zine culture
Microcosm grew into a hybrid of micro-press and indie publisher
producing and distributing hundreds of titles while still foregrounding small-press sensibilities like hand-drawn layouts and subcultural topics.

fields.name: Wyrd Sisters Distro
notes: Wyrd Sisters Distro is a Portland-based zine distro and record label focused specifically on neurodiverse and disabled artists

highlighted in distro directories as a dedicated platform for creators whose work is often marginalized even within DIY spaces. The distro's catalog concentrates on zines and music projects made by neurodivergent and disabled people
aligning its curation with disability justice and anti-ableist politics.

fields.name: Poopsheet Shop
notes: Poopsheet Shop is an online shop and archive project specializing in mini-comics
and related curiosities from the 1970s to the present
operating under the umbrella of the Poopsheet Foundation. It focuses heavily on small-press and self-published comics
often stocking rare or out-of-print items as well as new work by contemporary mini-comics artists.

fields.name: Mend My Dress Press
notes: Mend My Dress Press is a small
'grrrl-run' publishing house and zine distributor based in Tacoma
dedicated to anthologizing and amplifying zine culture. The press publishes collections of classic zines and related small art books—for example
anthologies of Doris by Cindy Crabb and Mend My Dress by Cristy C. Road—alongside original titles that maintain a distinctly DIY look and focus on feminism

fields.name: Sweet Candy Distro
notes: Sweet Candy Distro and Sweet Candy Press is a longstanding zine distro and small press founded and run by Sage Adderley
Washington and later noted in some library guides as Washington
DC. The distro has for over a decade carried a wide range of perzines
while the press side publishes original titles such as Ofrenda: A Zine Anthology by Celia Pérez.

fields.name: Neither-Nor
notes: Neither-nor Zine Distro is a Kansas City-based zine distro and zine library project founded in 2015 by Jess Hogan after the success of the first KC Zine Con. Hogan
a Kansas Citian who loves making
started Neither-nor to give local zinesters and enthusiasts a place to sell their zines
and build a sustainable zine destination in the city. The project has grown into a distro plus a collectively run zine library
which hosts a monthly Zine Club and participates actively in KC Zine Con.

fields.name: Sprout Zine Distro
notes: Sprout Zine Distro (often referenced simply as Sprout Distro) is a distro and resource project focused on anarchist and security-oriented zines
particularly those dealing with legal rights
and community defense. It appears in community-resource lists as a curated source for zines such as 'Threat Library' by the No Trace Project
along with other titles covering individual and collective safety

fields.name: Sticky Institute
notes: Long-running zine shop/artist-run space; a 'Melbourne institution' that has operated a zine shop since 2001 (originally in the Flinders St/Degraves subway; now in the Nicholas Building). They stock thousands of zines from around the world
80% of shelf price back to the artist in one interview)
and run major events like the Festival of the Photocopier and Australian Zine Showcase.

fields.name: Fight Boredom
notes: Long-running feminist/queer-leaning zine distro (originally associated with the Riot Grrrl DIY back-to-basics wave).

fields.name: Look Mum! Distro
notes: Canadian distro often carrying personal/political zines; historically present at zine fests and mail-order.

fields.name: Eskaramuza DIY Distro
notes: DIY music and zine distro and physical shop
Chile. Punk/metal/grindcore-leaning underground culture: they buy and sell CDs
and also fabricate musical merchandise (likely screen-printed shirts
etc.) for bands. Runs a bricks-and-mortar shop at O'Higgins 575 in Curicó and does mail-order.

fields.name: Vampire Hag Distro
notes: Full-size zine distro based in Chatham
described as 'the zine distro with a bite
' previously known as Vampire Sushi. Has been around since Halloween 2009
selling mostly queer and feminist perzines. The branding and social presence highlight a playful
goth-adjacent aesthetic centered on personal/political queer work.

fields.name: Black Star Books
notes: DIY politics; often carries political and queer zines).

fields.name: Zine COOP
notes: Collective that runs zine events and distribution
often focusing on Hong Kong/Asian independent publishing and politically sensitive work.

fields.name: Wahala Zine
notes: Lagos-based DIY zine platform centering African perspectives and youth culture; important for Global South representation.

fields.name: Queer Zine Archive Project
notes: Community archive founded 2003 to preserve queer zines and queer zine culture and make them digitally accessible. They maintain both a physical collection (thousands of zines stored in Milwaukee) and a searchable online archive with hundreds of freely downloadable digitized zines. Mission explicitly frames zines as living history and as a response to marginalization

fields.name: San Francisco Public Library Zine Collection
notes: Library collection documenting the Bay Area underground/alternative press and its impact on the city's cultural
and political life (good institutional anchor for West Coast radical/queer material).

fields.name: UMBC Sci-Fi & Fantasy Fanzines Collection
notes: Baltimore County collection focusing on SF/F fanzines; more genre than explicitly queer
but historically important for fan-culture zine history.

fields.name: Black Mosquito
notes: Not-for-profit anarchist mailorder based in Germany
radical-left and emancipatory ideas and practices; operates as a collective and explicitly channels all profit (after fixed costs) back into emancipatory projects. They stock stickers
and solidarity products like Zapatista coffee and olive oil from Greek anarchist collectives.

fields.name: Heavy Metal Zine Distro
notes: Berlin-based zine distro specializing in queer and feminist zines.

fields.name: Papiercafé
notes: Student-run zine/showroom space at the Kunsthochschule Kassel (Kassel Art School). Functions as a 'room for student publications
coffee and cake' at the art school
and zines by students. They host zine markets and showcase new titles from the school community.

fields.name: Mount Zine
notes: Mount Zine is a Tokyo-based zine project and shop where anyone can participate
framing itself as a space where 'anyone can publish a zine.' It operates a physical shop/gallery (most recently in Setagaya/Meguro areas) that specializes in zines and other small-run printed matter
taking in open submissions from creators in Japan and abroad and routinely stocking over 150-200 titles at a time
with all stock rotated roughly every six months. Beyond sales
they run zine-making workshops and a 'zine school
' host events and exhibitions in Japan and overseas

fields.name: Tokyo Art Book Fair
notes: Tokyo Art Book Fair (often abbreviated TABF) is Japan's first book fair dedicated to art publications
launched in 2009 under the name 'ZINE'S MATE: TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR' and now one of the largest art book and zine fairs in Asia. Held annually at venues such as the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo
it regularly hosts around 300 exhibitors from Japan and abroad and draws 20
with sections that explicitly foreground zines and independent/self-published work.

fields.name: Tijuana Zine Fest
notes: Tijuana Zine Fest is a large-scale
bilingual zine festival in downtown Tijuana that brings together DIY publishers
and artists from both sides of the U.S.-Mexico border. Founded by Luisa Martinez and David Peña to create a space for local zinesters to network and present their work
the fest is held in reclaimed pasajes off Avenida Revolución—passageways once dominated by tourist curio shops and later transformed into cultural corridors of galleries
and coffee shops after the height of drug-war violence. The event hosts well over a hundred independent publishers
creating a space for exchanging personal stories
and experimental visual work in both Spanish and English.

fields.name: Tonone Bookstore
notes: Tonone Bookstore (often written 'Tonone' or 'Tobay / Tonone Bookstore') is a small independent bookshop in Vientiane
located near That Luang and a local mini Big C at a three-way junction. Facebook activity shows them as a general bookstore carrying popular fiction
and translated titles. Functions more as an indie general bookstore that might be open to DIY material rather than a dedicated distro.

fields.name: Common Room PH
notes: Common Room PH is a Philippine collaborative space and retail platform for independent artists and makers
with multiple physical stores and an online presence that host locally made art
and zines. They describe themselves as providing 'a home and a safe space for creatives to express themselves
and empower others to make with their hands
' and they actively highlight storytelling and community-building as part of their mission.

fields.name: BAEK
notes: BAEK is a South African independent 'baking zine' and art project created by fine artist and baker Alice Toich
described as 'somewhere between a recipe book
art publication and fashion shoot.' The full-colour zine is positioned as a 'decadent' object that merges high-end food styling
and issues are mailed directly to subscribers.

fields.name: Sandwich Mixto
fields.address: Calle Torrecilla del Leal 7, Madrid, Spain
notes: Sandwich Mixto is a Madrid shop dedicated to fanzines and self-published work
originally operating as a stall in the Antón Martín market before moving to a street-level space on Calle Torrecilla del Leal 7. Run by Virginia del Diego
the store specializes in fanzines and uses its expanded wall space for detailed exhibitions that explore the entire fanzine-making process
from concept and sketches through printing and all the 'glitches' involved.

fields.name: Space Bar Zine
notes: SPACEBAR ZINE is an independent print and arts imprint under SPACEBAR Design Studio
focuses on independent printings and arts and also maintains online media for Thai artists and interested audiences
positioning itself as part design studio
